title: Fixing a bug, start to finish
blurb: One prompt: koda writes a plan, reads the file, shows the edit as a diff before it lands, marks the plan done, and reports what changed.

title: /help
blurb: Every command with an example of it in use, and the keys, in two panels.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
blurb: The whole keymap, from inside koda, with /keys.

title: Eleven palettes, switched live
blurb: The block fills, the context gauge and the mode chip re-tint together, because they are drawn from the palette rather than hard-coded.

title: Plan, execute, vibe
blurb: ctrl+p cycles autonomy; /mode opens the picker. Plan mode cannot write, and says so instead of asking.

title: Nothing is written without you
blurb: The default tier shows the diff and waits: y allows once, a always allows this tool, n declines.

title: Putting a file back
blurb: /undo restores the last file the agent changed, from koda's own copy — not from git.

title: Delegating to a subagent
blurb: A wide search costs a paragraph of context instead of thirty files: the subagent reads, and reports back.

title: Watching it think
blurb: Reasoning tokens are shown separately from the answer, and ctrl+t expands the last block.

title: When it needs a decision
blurb: ask_user opens a dropdown in the middle of the screen — the answer goes where the question is.

title: Stopping a run
blurb: ctrl+c stops the turn and keeps what streamed; twice quits.

title: Every tool it can call
blurb: /tools lists what is wired in right now, including anything from your koda.toml.

title: The command palette
blurb: Type / and the list filters as you go; tab completes.

title: Attaching a file with @
blurb: @ opens a fuzzy picker over the repo; the file is attached to the message, not pasted into it.

title: Running a command yourself
blurb: ! runs a shell command and $ runs Python, both without spending a turn on the model.

title: What it has been doing
blurb: /logs opens the activity log over the transcript: every tool call, with timings.

title: Compacting the context
blurb: /compact replaces the conversation so far with a summary of it, and hands the tokens back — the gauge on the status bar moves as it lands.

title: Headless: koda -p, in any mode
blurb: No TUI: -p streams the answer to stdout and exits, and --mode picks how much it is allowed to do.

title: When the server refuses native tool calls
blurb: koda tries native tool calls, and falls back to <tool_call> text blocks on a 400 — the turn continues instead of failing.

title: Finding a symbol without grepping
blurb: The code graph answers where a symbol is defined and who calls it, from an index koda keeps itself.

title: Remembering how your project works
blurb: What it learns from a turn is written down, and carried into the next session.

title: Project rules, loaded only when they apply
blurb: A skill costs about fifteen tokens until it is relevant; then the agent reads the whole thing.

title: Your own commands as tools
blurb: A shell command declared in koda.toml is called like a built-in — and shows up in /tools.

title: Reading a spreadsheet with @
blurb: CSV, PDF, Word and Excel are parsed to text on the way in, so @ works on more than source files.

title: Acting on an AI! comment
blurb: With watch on, koda picks up an AI! comment the moment you save the file — no prompt typed.

title: Every past conversation
blurb: /resume reopens one, /search finds one by what was said in it, /fork branches it.

title: Everything, editable in place
blurb: /settings is the whole config file as a screen: arrows move, space toggles, ctrl+s saves.

title: Pointing it at a model
blurb: /models lists what the server actually has; /model switches, and /setup changes the endpoint.

title: How much it may do unasked
blurb: /auto cycles ask → auto-write → full-auto, and the tier is on the status bar the whole time.

title: How hard it thinks
blurb: /reason sets the effort a reasoning model spends before it answers.

title: A real debugger, driven by the agent
blurb: Breakpoints, stepping and live variables over the Debug Adapter Protocol — this is a real debugpy session, not a print statement.

title: Pointing koda at your server
blurb: /setup walks the endpoint, the model and the key, and writes the config for you.

title: First run, from the shell
blurb: The three commands that tell you the install worked: the version, the models your server reports, and one real answer.

title: Searching the web
blurb: Off by default; on, the query really goes to DuckDuckGo (or your SearXNG) and the results come back as a tool result you can read.

title: Driving a real browser
blurb: For pages that only exist after JavaScript runs: a real Chromium, with the page's interactive elements indexed so the agent can click them.

title: Serving the web control center
blurb: web_ui = true makes koda serve its trace waterfall and prompt inspector on 127.0.0.1 — loopback only, and only alongside the TUI: a headless `-p` run starts no server, as this shows.
